column1: # tools/suite-map.tsv — which suites cover which changed path. The ONLY place affected-only selection is
# decided: the fast gate runs the suites named here for a changed file, and FAILS LOUDLY when a changed file
# maps to none, because a changed module that maps to zero suites is a false green.
#   <glob><TAB><suite> [<suite> ...]     a changed path matching <glob> runs those suites
#   !<glob>                              EXEMPT: no suite can cover this path
#   * Globs are bash patterns tested with `[[ $path == $glob ]]`, so `*` also crosses `/`.
#   * A changed file under tests/ that is itself a suite maps to ITSELF, before this file is consulted.
#   * A row beats an exemption. A source file with several covering suites must list ALL of them: the
#     surviving suites prove nothing about the omitted one (the full gate on the merged union is the only
#   * ONE MODULE PER ROW, deliberately: a directory-wide row would claim that suites written before a module
#     existed cover that module too. A new module is UNMAPPED until its author names its suites.
# One row per module, so a NEW module is unmapped until its author names the suites that cover it. main.ts is
# the boot file and content.ts/feed.ts/server.ts are the application (full-rss-11b, the ADR full-rss-7d0).
# --- the gate itself is code, and it has its own suite -------------------------------------------------
# The full-gate wrapper is what the merger and CI run, so tools/fast-gate.test.sh exercises its two steps
# (with stub commands) as well as the fast gate's selection. Editing the suite itself maps to itself.
# --- a dependency change can invalidate any suite, so claim every suite -------------------------------
